subject: pathology
title: Pneumoconioses and environmental lung disease

steps.tx: **Pneumoconioses** are lung fibroses caused by inhaled inorganic dusts retained in lungs over years of occupational exposure at work. Coal dust, silica and asbestos are the classic agents, while fibre shape, durability and total dose decide how pathogenic exposure becomes eventually. Disease may progress after exposure ends because retained particles continue stimulating inflammation and fibrosis inside lung tissue for years afterwards. **Occupational history** therefore functions as a diagnostic test that imaging alone can never replace in clinic.
steps.say: Pneumoconiosis is a fibrotic disease where inorganic dust accumulates in lungs during years of occupational exposure at mines or factories. Retained particles matter because durable fibres keep stimulating macrophages long after exposure stops outside workplace environments completely and permanently. Job history helps clinicians connect imaging patterns with specific dust exposures retrospectively.

steps.tx: **Silicosis** follows quartz inhalation during mining, stone cutting and sandblasting work where respirable silica reaches alveoli in large amounts daily. Fibrosis favours upper lobes with small nodules, hilar **eggshell calcification** and progressive massive fibrosis in heavily exposed workers over time. Silica impairs macrophage killing, so tuberculosis reactivates readily inside damaged lungs and creates silicotuberculosis in endemic settings frequently encountered. Acute silicoproteinosis follows massive exposure within months and resembles alveolar proteinosis clinically and radiologically in presentation.
steps.say: Silicosis is a disease where quartz dust scars upper lobes and calcifies hilar nodes in an eggshell pattern radiologically over years of exposure. Macrophage injury occurs because silica damages phagolysosomes and impairs killing of inhaled tuberculosis bacilli inside alveolar macrophages after ingestion attempts fail repeatedly. Heavy exposure helps clinicians anticipate progressive massive fibrosis in miners.

steps.tx: **Asbestosis** fibroses lower lobes in a subpleural distribution and marks exposure through pleural plaques, thickening and effusions on imaging studies. Ferruginous asbestos bodies on biopsy prove exposure, although malignancy risk matters more than fibrosis burden for long term patient outcomes overall. Smoking multiplies **lung cancer** risk, while **mesothelioma** develops decades after exposure even when fibrosis remains relatively limited in extent. Lower lobe disease therefore separates asbestosis from upper lobe silicosis in classic exam comparisons.
steps.say: Asbestosis is a disease where inhaled fibres scar lower lobes and thicken pleura over decades after workplace exposure ends completely for retired workers. Plaques indicate exposure because pleural calcification records earlier fibre deposition without necessarily causing breathlessness by itself in many screened individuals attending follow up clinics. Cancer risk matters because mesothelioma develops decades later.

steps.tx: This lung histology shows golden brown beaded **asbestos bodies** lying inside tissue that is thickened by pink interstitial fibrosis around them. The magnified inset reveals the segmented ferruginous coating that forms when macrophages coat inhaled asbestos fibres with iron rich protein over years. These bodies prove asbestos exposure, while the surrounding **interstitial fibrosis** shows actual asbestosis rather than exposure alone without disease. Examiners use this image because exposure markers and fibrotic damage appear together in one field.
steps.say: This histology shows asbestos bodies because macrophages coat inhaled fibres with iron rich protein and create beaded golden structures inside lung tissue permanently after exposure. Interstitial fibrosis appears because surrounding alveolar walls thicken with pink collagen between airspaces in lower lobe disease patterns typically sampled. Exposure proof helps clinicians attribute fibrosis correctly.

steps.tx: **Coal workers pneumoconiosis** ranges from simple black macules with little impairment to progressive massive fibrosis in a minority of miners. Simple disease causes limited symptoms, while massive fibrosis produces disabling restriction and **cor pulmonale** when pulmonary vessels become destroyed extensively. Mixed silica exposure changes the pattern, so pure coal disease lacks the eggshell calcification that suggests silicosis on imaging studies. **Caplan syndrome** adds rheumatoid necrobiotic nodules erupting inside pneumoconiotic lungs of patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
steps.say: Coal disease is a spectrum where simple macules cause little impairment while massive fibrosis disables a minority of miners after prolonged dust exposure underground over decades working in pits. Caplan syndrome develops because rheumatoid nodules erupt inside lungs already scarred by inhaled coal dust particles retained permanently in tissue macrophages and interstitium. Restriction occurs because massive conglomerates replace compliant lung.

steps.tx: **Hypersensitivity pneumonitis** is immune alveolitis caused by organic antigens rather than inorganic mineral fibrosis from occupational dust inhalation over years. Farmer lung follows mouldy hay, bird fancier lung follows avian proteins, and hot tub lung follows mycobacterial exposure in contaminated water systems. Acute episodes cause fever and breathlessness hours after exposure, while chronic disease fibroses upper and mid zones with mosaic attenuation on scans. **Antigen avoidance** treats disease and also tests the diagnosis when symptoms settle away from exposure.
steps.say: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is an immune disease where organic antigens inflame alveoli hours after exposure in sensitised workers or hobbyists exposed at home environments repeatedly during seasons. Fever develops because immune reactions release cytokines after antigen inhalation reaches distal airspaces and alveolar walls diffusely throughout both lungs causing systemic symptoms. Avoidance helps clinicians confirm causation when symptoms settle.
